Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — reranking use case

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call today — really helpful to walk through how Redwood handles reranking for our product search. Quick recap from our side and a couple of follow-ups: 

- Our goal: improve SERP relevance for commerce search, reduce time-to-click, and improve conversion on query-driven recommendations.
- Traffic: ~200M queries/month; peak concurrent QPS ~800.
- Current infra: internal rerank model (bi-encoder + pairwise reranker) with extraction latency ~120ms; looking to reduce tail latency and cost per 1M queries.

Immediate asks:
1) Can you share the NDCG/MRR benchmark profile you referenced for the candidate models?
2) Example prompt sets or evaluation queries that map to our catalog structure (we can sanitize)
3) A proposed A/B plan (metrics, sample size, rollout cadence)

If you can send the benchmark spreadsheet and a recommended next step plan, we can sync with engineering and procurement next week.

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Johnson
Head of Search, Acme Commerce
alex.johnson@acme.com
From: marissa_cole
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: priya.singh@acme.com, rishi_malhotra, neha_kapoor
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — reranking use case

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the specific asks. Attaching the NDCG/MRR export I mentioned and a sanitized prompt set we use for rerank validation. High level notes up front:

- Recommended models: redwood/rerank-base-v2 (good latency/cost balance) and redwood/rerank-highrec-q8 (higher quality, quantized, slightly higher tail latency)
- Benchmarks attached (acme_ndcg_mrr_results.xlsx): synthetic evaluation vs. our standard ecom prompt set (attached prompt_set_v1.csv). These are held-out queries from a retail catalog and include typical reformulations.
- Key risk: potential quality regression on long-tail queries that rely heavily on user signals (session features). We recommend a small feature parity validation before A/B.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) We (Redwood) run a 2-week offline validation against your anonymized query logs (sample of 100k queries) to compute NDCG@10 and MRR; share full spreadsheet.
2) If metrics look good, run a 2-week online A/B with 10% traffic (control: current model, treatment: rerank-base-v2). Primary metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, click-through rate (CTR), and delta in average latency and P99 latency.
3) If treatment improves NDCG/MRR by >= 3% without >10ms increase in P95 tail, expand to 30% and prepare rollout.

I attached a one-pager mutual action plan (MAP) and a proposed timeline. We'll also surface an estimated cost delta for the Dedicated option vs hosted per 100M queries.

I'll loop Rishi (ML infra) and Neha (sales ops) on specifics for instrumentation and procurement.

Would 10am PT Thursday for a short engineering sync work?

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: rishi_malhotra

Adding a few engineering notes on the offline validation and the A/B plan: 

- Offline validation: for fairness, we'll score both your current reranker and the candidate models with exactly the same features and input tokens. Please provide the sanitized sample (ideally as CSV with query, candidate_docs, click_label). We can accept up to 200k rows; 100k is reasonable to start.
- Metrics: we'll compute NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, and per-query latency distribution (mean, p50, p90, p95, p99).
- A/B plan: target 10% initial traffic; instrumentation should capture user_id hashed, query_id, timestamp, treatment flag, rank list and click events. We'll provide a schema for logs.
- Tagging: add a request param (x-redwood-rerank-treatment: acme-2026-08-v1) to make offline->online mapping easier.

I'll run the first pass offline once we have the CSV. If possible, prioritize a slice of queries that historically had low CTR — that's where rerank often produces the biggest gains.

-rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
ML Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
